points: A batch job processes a fixed pile of data and finishes, while a stream job runs continuously on data that never ends and answers as events arrive.
Because events arrive late and out of order, a stream job uses a watermark to decide when a window of event time is complete.
Lambda keeps a streaming job and a separate batch job that must agree, while Kappa reruns the one streaming job over stored history.
Uber reads a Hive table as a streaming source, two hours of data per trigger, so the window size limits the load on Kafka and the sinks.
Netflix keeps events in Iceberg as well as Kafka and swaps the source for backfills, which it found far cheaper than long Kafka retention.

figures.label: Retaining 30 days of events in Kafka was estimated at 93 million dollars a year
Netflix's backfill output matched production output at 99.9%
Uber says a backfill can cover a few days of data in one day

prerequisiteReasons.log-based-streaming: A stream job reads from a log and relies on being able to read it again from an earlier position, which is the idea that backfill builds on.
